question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(In fact, climbing fern is spreading so rapidly that its) now the state's worst invasive weed.
option_1: In fact, climbing fern is spreading so rapid that it's
option_2: In fact, climbing fern is spread so rapidly that its
option_3: In fact, climbing fern is spreading so rapidly that it's
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. In fact, climbing fern is spreading so rapidly that it's.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed part contains one clear error — the word "its" — and only Option 3 corrects it while keeping the rest of the segment intact.

◦ The clause after "that" needs a subject + verb: "... that it is now the state's worst invasive weed." The contraction of "it is" is "it's" (with an apostrophe).

◦ "Its" (without apostrophe) is a possessive adjective (belonging to it) and cannot work as "subject + verb" before the adverb "now". (इसका / अपना)

◦ The rest of the segment is already correct: "is spreading" (present continuous, for a process going on now) and "so rapidly" (adverb rapidly modifying the verb "is spreading").

◦ Correct sentence: In fact, climbing fern is spreading so rapidly that it's now the state's worst invasive weed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spreading so rapid" is wrong — an adverb (rapidly), not the adjective "rapid", is needed to modify the verb "is spreading".

• Option 2 "is spread" changes the meaning to passive/past and also keeps the wrong "its".

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed segment carries the "its / it's" error.

NOTE

• Remember the pair: its = belonging to it (The tree shed its leaves); it's = it is / it has (It's raining; It's been a long day).

• Adjective vs adverb: adjectives describe nouns (a rapid spread), adverbs describe verbs/adjectives/adverbs (spreading rapidly). This pair is a very common SSC trap.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Consensus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Consensus" — c-o-n-s-e-n-s-u-s — with an "s" in the middle and "-sus" at the end.

◦ Consensus (noun) means a general agreement among all the members of a group. (सर्वसम्मति)

◦ Example: The committee finally reached a consensus on the new policy.

◦ Memory tip: consensus comes from Latin consentire = to feel together, and is related to "consent" and "sense" — both spelt with s, never with "c" in the middle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Concensus" is a very common misspelling caused by confusing it with the word "census".

• Option 2 "Concencus" and Option 4 "Consencus" both wrongly use "c" in place of "s".

• Do not confuse consensus (agreement) with census (official count of population).

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "reach/arrive at a consensus", "a consensus of opinion", "consensus candidate".

• Other frequently misspelt SSC words of this family: conscience, conscious, consistent, consecutive.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the (bracketed) word in the given sentence.

It would effectively rouse people's ardour to invest, and help to (discourage) the transfer of capital abroad.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Persuade.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed word is "discourage", which means to try to prevent something / to take away someone's confidence or willingness to do something. (हतोत्साहित करना)

◦ Its antonym must convey the idea of urging or convincing someone to do something.

◦ "Persuade" means to make somebody do something by giving them good reasons; to convince. (मनाना / राजी करना) It is therefore the opposite of "discourage" among the given options.

◦ The sentence talks of rousing people's ardour (enthusiasm) to invest, so the second half logically needs a positive word too.

◦ Correct: ... it would rouse people's ardour to invest, and help to persuade the transfer of capital abroad.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Industrious" (adjective) = hard-working, diligent. It is not an antonym of discourage.

• Option 2 "Construe" = to interpret or understand something in a particular way.

• Option 4 "Intolerable" (adjective) = unbearable, too bad to be endured.

NOTE

• Synonyms of discourage: dishearten, deter, dissuade, demoralise, dampen.

• Antonyms of discourage: encourage, persuade, urge, inspire, hearten, motivate.

• "Ardour" used in the sentence itself means great enthusiasm or passion.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice

This ______ piece of mischief by his brother brought a quiet laugh from David.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. whimsical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Whimsical" means playfully odd, quaint or fanciful; done on a sudden impulse for fun. (सनकी / अजीब और मज़ाकिया)

◦ The clue in the sentence is "brought a quiet laugh from David" — the mischief was amusing and harmlessly odd, not stupid or offensive.

◦ A whimsical piece of mischief is exactly the kind of light-hearted prank that makes someone smile quietly.

◦ Correct: This whimsical piece of mischief by his brother brought a quiet laugh from David.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "nonsensical" = absurd, having no meaning or sense; it carries a negative tone and would not naturally produce an affectionate laugh.

• Option 2 "classical" = relating to ancient Greek/Roman culture or to serious traditional art and music; it does not fit "mischief".

• Option 4 "vesical" is a medical adjective meaning relating to the urinary bladder — completely out of context.

NOTE

• Word family: whim (a sudden wish), whimsy (playful oddness), whimsical (adjective), whimsically (adverb).

• In such fill-in-the-blank questions, first locate the tone indicator in the sentence (here "a quiet laugh") and then choose the option matching that tone.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

The life and soul of the party
option_1: The only person who dances in the party
option_3: A person who brings lots of gifts
option_4: Person who brings lots of energy to the party
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Person who brings lots of energy to the party.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the life and soul of the party" refers to the liveliest, most entertaining and most enthusiastic person in a gathering — the one whose energy keeps everybody cheerful. (महफिल की जान)

◦ "Life" and "soul" together stand for spirit and energy, so the phrase describes the source of fun and vitality in a group.

◦ Example: Ravi is always the life and soul of the party — he sings, jokes and gets everyone dancing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong — the idiom is not about dancing alone; it is about overall liveliness.

• Option 2 "Chief guest" refers to a position of honour, not to a lively personality.

• Option 3 "a person who brings lots of gifts" is a literal, incorrect reading of the phrase.

NOTE

• Related idioms often asked in SSC exams: a wet blanket (a person who spoils others' fun), a party pooper (one who spoils a party), paint the town red (to celebrate wildly), let one's hair down (to relax and enjoy).

• Idioms must always be learnt as whole units — their meaning cannot be worked out from the individual words.

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correct spelt words.
option_1: The main problem, I beleive, lies elsewhere.
option_2: He said the goverment remained commited to peace.
option_3: You could have seen in them a cemetery or a war memorial.
option_4: Jerry is an amatuer who dances because he feels like it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. You could have seen in them a cemetery or a war memorial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Option 3 every word is spelt correctly — "cemetery" (c-e-m-e-t-e-r-y, with three e's and no 'a') and "memorial" are both accurate.

◦ Cemetery = a burial ground / graveyard. (कब्रिस्तान)

◦ Memorial = a structure built in memory of a person or event. (स्मारक)

◦ The other three options each contain at least one misspelt word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — "beleive" is wrong; the correct spelling is "believe" (remember the rule: i before e except after c).

• Option 2 — two errors: "goverment" should be "government" (keep the n of govern), and "commited" should be "committed" (double t).

• Option 4 — "amatuer" is wrong; the correct spelling is "amateur" (a-m-a-t-e-u-r).

NOTE

• Doubling rule: in words like commit → committed / committing and prefer → preferred, the final consonant is doubled when the last syllable is stressed.

• Other high-frequency SSC spellings: occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, necessary, privilege, recommend, separate.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Early, during December 2021, / Lal was appointed as / the Secretary to the Lokpal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Early, during December 2021,

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the use of "Early" instead of the comparative form "Earlier".

◦ To mean "at some time before now / previously", English uses the adverb "earlier": Earlier, during December 2021, ...

◦ "Early" means near the beginning of a period, or before the expected time (He came early; early in the morning). It cannot introduce a past reference in this way.

◦ Corrected sentence: Earlier, during December 2021, Lal was appointed as the Secretary to the Lokpal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment "Lal was appointed as" is correct — passive voice in the simple past (was + past participle) suits an official appointment.

• Segment "the Secretary to the Lokpal." is correct — the definite article the is properly used with a unique post and with the institution Lokpal.

• Note that "appointed as + post" and "appointed + post" are both acceptable in standard usage.

NOTE

• Compare: early (adjective/adverb of time) vs earlier (comparative) vs soon (in a short time from now).

• The Lokpal is India's apex anti-corruption ombudsman body, set up under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 — useful for the General Awareness paper as well.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Neither I nor my friends are going too walk down that street.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. friends are going too walk

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the word "too", which must be replaced by the infinitive marker "to".

◦ The structure required is "be going to + base verb" (near-future): are going to walk.

◦ "Too" is an adverb meaning also or excessively (He is too tired; She came too) and can never be used before a base verb in this structure.

◦ Corrected sentence: Neither I nor my friends are going to walk down that street.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The verb form "are" is correct here because of the proximity rule (rule of the nearest subject): with neither ... nor / either ... or, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it — here the plural "my friends".

• Segment "Neither I nor my" is correct — neither is properly paired with nor.

• Segment "down that street." is correct — the preposition "down" is idiomatic with streets and roads.

NOTE

• Homophone trap: to (preposition/infinitive marker), too (also/excessively), two (the number 2).

• Correlative pairs to remember: either–or, neither–nor, both–and, not only–but also, whether–or.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew / its top, burying the ancient / cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.
option_1: In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In 79 A.D., the Mount Vesuvius blew

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the definite article "the" before "Mount Vesuvius".

◦ Names of individual mountains/peaks do not take "the": Mount Everest, Mount Vesuvius, Mount Fuji, Kanchenjunga.

◦ "The" is used with mountain ranges (the Himalayas, the Alps, the Andes, the Western Ghats), not with a single mountain.

◦ Corrected sentence: In 79 A.D., Mount Vesuvius blew its top, burying the ancient cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "its top, burying the ancient" is correct — the possessive "its" (no apostrophe) is right, and "burying" is a correct participial phrase showing a simultaneous result.

• Segment "cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum." is correct — no article is needed before the names of these cities.

• The idiom "blow its top" here means to erupt violently.

NOTE

• Article rules worth memorising: the with ranges, rivers, seas, oceans, deserts, groups of islands; no article with single mountains, single islands, lakes (Lake Chilika), continents and most countries.

• Fact: the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 A.D. buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum in Italy.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

This change is responsible for a recent ______ the number of cases of cancer in this age group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rise in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed prepositional collocation is "a rise in something" when we speak of an increase in an amount, number, level or price.

◦ Correct: a rise in prices, a rise in temperature, a rise in the number of cases.

◦ Corrected sentence: This change is responsible for a recent rise in the number of cases of cancer in this age group.

◦ The same pattern applies to increase in, fall in, decline in, drop in, growth in.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rise to" is used for the level reached, as in "a rise to 40 degrees" or the phrase "rise to power".

• Option 2 "rise at" is not a standard collocation with a countable quantity like this.

• Option 4 "rise of" indicates the size of the increase (a rise of 10 per cent) or the emergence of something (the rise of nationalism) — not the thing that is increasing.

NOTE

• Remember the trio: a rise of 5% (amount of change) — a rise in prices (what changed) — a rise to ₹50 (final level).

• SSC frequently tests such noun + preposition pairs: demand for, cure for, remedy for, solution to, answer to, reason for, cause of, effect on.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

For months, Drupad could not taste anything he ate as regret layered ______ mud.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. his mouth like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs a simile — a comparison between the coating of regret and mud — and the natural word for a comparison before a noun is "like".

◦ Structure: verb + object + like + noun → "regret layered his mouth like mud".

◦ "Like" is a preposition here, and prepositions are followed by nouns/noun phrases ('mud'), which fits perfectly.

◦ Corrected sentence: For months, Drupad could not taste anything he ate as regret layered his mouth like mud.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "as though" is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), e.g. "as though it were mud" — not by the bare noun "mud".

• Option 3 "comparable to" is formal and unidiomatic in this literary sentence, and it does not fit the verb "layered".

• Option 4 "allied to" means connected or related to and makes no sense with 'mud'.

NOTE

• Rule of thumb: like + noun/pronoun (He runs like a deer); as + clause (He runs as his father did).

• A simile uses like/as; a metaphor states the comparison directly (Regret was mud in his mouth).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A local meeting of party members to select candidates, elect convention delegates, etc
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Caucus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "caucus" is a meeting of the members or leaders of a political party to choose candidates, decide policy or elect delegates. (राजनीतिक दल की बैठक)

◦ It exactly matches the definition given: "a local meeting of party members to select candidates, elect convention delegates, etc."

◦ Example: The party held a caucus to pick its nominee for the election.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Claque" = a group of people hired to applaud a performer or speaker.

• Option 2 "Clique" = a small exclusive group of people who do not readily allow others to join them.

• Option 3 "Caravan" = a group of people travelling together, especially across a desert, or a covered vehicle for living in.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutions from politics often asked in SSC: quorum (minimum members needed for a valid meeting), referendum (a direct vote by the people on a single issue), coalition (a temporary alliance of parties), plebiscite (a public vote on a major issue).

• In the USA, the Iowa caucuses are a famous example of this system.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

The flowers of a particular region
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Flora.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flora" means the plants and flowers of a particular region, habitat or period. (किसी क्षेत्र की वनस्पति)

◦ Example: The Western Ghats are famous for their rich flora and fauna.

◦ The word comes from Flora, the Roman goddess of flowers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Fauna" = the animals of a particular region — the natural partner-word of flora.

• Option 3 "Bovine" = relating to cattle (cows and oxen); as an adjective it can also mean slow or dull.

• Option 4 "Bryophyte" = a non-vascular plant such as moss or liverwort, only one small group of plants and not the flowers of a whole region.

NOTE

• Learn the pair together: flora (plants) and fauna (animals); avifauna refers specifically to the birds of a region.

• Related one-word substitutions: herbarium (a collection of dried plants), arboretum (a garden of trees), apiary (a place where bees are kept), aviary (a large cage for birds).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Console
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Solace.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Console" (verb) means to comfort somebody who is unhappy or disappointed. (सांत्वना देना)

◦ "Solace" can be used as both a noun (comfort in sorrow) and a verb (to give comfort to), so it is the closest synonym among the options.

◦ Example: She tried to console / solace the weeping child.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Fret" = to worry or be anxious, the opposite idea.

• Option 2 "Arteriole" = a small branch of an artery — a medical term, unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4 "Torment" = to cause severe physical or mental suffering — an antonym of console.

NOTE

• Synonyms of console: comfort, soothe, solace, assuage, cheer up.

• Antonyms of console: torment, distress, upset, agitate, torture.

• Do not confuse the verb console (kun-SOHL) with the noun console (KON-sohl — a control panel or a gaming device).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Each passenger is allows one piece of carry-on luggage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is allowed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence must be in the passive voice, because the passenger receives the permission — he does not allow anything himself.

◦ Passive structure = be + past participle (V3) → "is allowed".

◦ The underlined "is allows" is wrong because a finite verb (allows) can never follow the auxiliary "is".

◦ The singular verb "is" is correct, since "Each passenger" is singular (each + singular noun + singular verb).

◦ Corrected sentence: Each passenger is allowed one piece of carry-on luggage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because the printed form "is allows" is clearly ungrammatical.

• Option 3 "is allowing" is present continuous active — it would wrongly mean the passenger is permitting something.

• Option 4 "is allow" is wrong because the base form cannot follow "is"; a participle is required.

NOTE

• Verb forms of allow: allow – allowed – allowed – allowing.

• Determiners each, every, either, neither, one of are always followed by a singular verb: Each of the boys is present.

• Common passive patterns: is given, is asked, is offered, is permitted, is granted — all with the third form of the verb.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Malign
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Praise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Malign" (verb) means to say bad or harmful things about somebody; to speak ill of / defame. (बदनाम करना)

◦ As an adjective it means evil or harmful in influence (a malign influence).

◦ Its clear antonym is "Praise" — to express approval or admiration for somebody. (प्रशंसा करना)

◦ Example: He was maligned by his rivals, but his teachers always praised his honesty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Align" = to arrange things in a straight line or to bring into agreement; it merely looks similar to 'malign'.

• Option 3 "Cheerful" = happy and positive; it is an adjective describing mood, not the opposite of defaming someone.

• Option 4 "Harangue" = a long, aggressive speech / to lecture someone angrily — closer in spirit to malign than opposite to it.

NOTE

• Synonyms of malign: defame, slander, vilify, denigrate, disparage, libel.

• Antonyms of malign: praise, commend, laud, extol, eulogise, compliment.

• Note the prefix mal- = bad/ill: malnutrition, malfunction, malpractice, malevolent, malicious.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice.

During treatment, patients lay ______ on the treatment couch for around 3 hrs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. supine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Supine" means lying flat on the back with the face turned upwards. (पीठ के बल लेटा हुआ)

◦ It fits perfectly with "lay ... on the treatment couch", which describes the posture of the patients.

◦ Corrected sentence: During treatment, patients lay supine on the treatment couch for around 3 hrs.

◦ Its opposite is "prone" — lying face downwards.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "arsine" is a poisonous gas (AsH₃) — a chemistry term, not a posture.

• Option 2 "alpine" = relating to high mountains, especially the Alps.

• Option 3 "repine" = to complain or fret discontentedly — a verb, so it cannot describe how patients lay.

NOTE

• Posture words worth remembering: supine (on the back), prone (on the front), recumbent (lying down), erect/upright (standing).

• "Supine" also has a figurative meaning — failing to act through moral weakness or laziness (a supine acceptance of injustice).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

Later, Brooks' brother alleged that racism helped put the (pedal to the metal).
option_2: To go full speed, especially while driving a vehicle
option_3: To enjoy yourself by going out
option_4: Avoid responsibility by giving it to someone else
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To go full speed, especially while driving a vehicle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "put the pedal to the metal" means to press the accelerator right down to the floor — i.e., to drive very fast or to do something at full speed / with maximum effort. (पूरी रफ़्तार से चलना)

◦ The image is of the accelerator pedal being pushed down to the metal floor of the vehicle.

◦ Example: We were running late, so he put the pedal to the metal and reached in twenty minutes.

◦ By extension it is also used for speeding up any activity — as in the given sentence about the pace of events.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Very excessive" is only a vague adjective phrase and does not capture the idea of speed.

• Option 3 "To enjoy yourself by going out" is the meaning of idioms like paint the town red.

• Option 4 "Avoid responsibility by giving it to someone else" is the meaning of pass the buck.

NOTE

• Other speed-related idioms: step on the gas (accelerate), in the fast lane (a busy, exciting life), at breakneck speed (dangerously fast), hell for leather (as fast as possible).

• In SSC papers, idioms are asked both as meaning and as fill in the blanks, so learn the exact wording of each idiom.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

He (returned back) Cambridge shortly before three o'clock.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. reached.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Returned back" is a redundant (pleonastic) expression, because the verb "return" already contains the sense of "back". Such repetition is a grammatical error.

◦ Moreover, "return" needs the preposition to before a place (returned to Cambridge), whereas the sentence has no preposition.

◦ The verb "reach" is transitive — it takes a direct object without any preposition: reached Cambridge, reached home, reached the station.

◦ Corrected sentence: He reached Cambridge shortly before three o'clock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "showed" needs an object or the particle 'up' (showed up at Cambridge) and is wrong as given.

• Option 2 "No correction required" is wrong because "returned back" is redundant and unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "appeared" would require a preposition (appeared in/at Cambridge) and does not convey arrival.

NOTE

• Common redundancies tested by SSC: return back, repeat again, revert back, join together, ascend up, descend down, free gift, final conclusion, new innovation.

• Verbs that take a direct object without a preposition: reach, enter, discuss, marry, resemble, order, attack, accompany.

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed part given in the sentence below.

I suppose I was looking for (a work that would give me income) and that was going to be an adventure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Occupation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Occupation" means a job or profession — the regular work by which a person earns a living. (व्यवसाय / रोज़गार)

◦ The bracketed part is "a work that would give me income", and the essential idea in it is earning money, which only "occupation" carries directly.

◦ Correct: I suppose I was looking for an occupation and that was going to be an adventure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Activity" = anything that a person does; it says nothing about income.

• Option 2 "Calling" = a strong inner urge or vocation to do a particular kind of work — it stresses inclination, not earnings.

• Option 3 "Pursuit" = an activity followed as a hobby or interest, or the act of chasing something.

NOTE

• Related vocabulary: profession (needs special training — law, medicine), vocation (work one feels called to), livelihood (means of supporting oneself), avocation (a hobby beside one's main work).

• In such questions, first identify the key idea in the bracketed phrase (here: income) and then match it with the option that contains that idea.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Intriguingly, those who (1)______ the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared (2)______ those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly (3)______ followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who (4)______ more psychobiotic foods during the four-week period reporting the (5)______ reduction in perceived stress levels.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. followed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a verb that goes with the noun "diet". The standard collocation in English is "to follow a diet" — meaning to eat according to a particular diet plan.

◦ The same verb is used later in the very same passage: "... those who followed the control diet" and "how strictly participants followed the diet", which confirms the choice.

◦ Correct: Intriguingly, those who followed the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "casted" is not a standard form at all — the past tense of cast is cast (cast – cast – cast), and it means to throw or to assign a role.

• Option 3 "believed" cannot take "the diet" as its object in this sense.

• Option 4 "bellowed" = shouted loudly in a deep voice, which is meaningless here.

NOTE

• Collocations with diet: follow / stick to / go on / be on a diet; a balanced diet; a strict diet.

• In cloze tests, always scan the rest of the passage — the writer usually repeats the same verb or structure elsewhere, as happens here with "followed".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Intriguingly, those who (1)______ the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared (2)______ those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly (3)______ followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who (4)______ more psychobiotic foods during the four-week period reporting the (5)______ reduction in perceived stress levels.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The required structure is "compared with", which is used when two things are set side by side to note similarities and differences.

◦ Here one group (those on the psychobiotic diet) is being measured against another group (those on the control diet), so "compared with" is the precise choice.

◦ Correct: ... they felt less stressed compared with those who followed the control diet.

◦ In research and statistical writing, "compared with" is the standard form for such contrasts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "compared of" is not an English collocation at all.

• Option 3 "compared by" would wrongly suggest who did the comparing (the agent).

• Option 4 "compared on" is used only with a basis of comparison (compared on the basis of price), which is not the sense here.

NOTE

• Compare with = examine similarities and differences (statistical/technical contrast).

• Compare to = liken one thing to another (Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?).

• Other useful prepositional pairs: differ from, similar to, superior to, inferior to, preferable to.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Intriguingly, those who (1)______ the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared (2)______ those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly (3)______ followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who (4)______ more psychobiotic foods during the four-week period reporting the (5)______ reduction in perceived stress levels.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. participants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage describes a dietary study/experiment, and the people who take part in such a study are called "participants" (also called subjects or volunteers). (प्रतिभागी)

◦ The blank is the subject of the verb "followed the diet", so it must be the group of people on the diet.

◦ Correct: There was also a direct correlation between how strictly participants followed the diet and their perceived stress levels.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "nomads" = people who move from place to place rather than settling; irrelevant to a diet trial.

• Option 3 "animals" is wrong — the passage clearly reports what people reported about their own perceived stress levels.

• Option 4 "spectators" = people who watch an event; they take no part in it, so they cannot follow the diet.

NOTE

• Research vocabulary useful for comprehension passages: control group (the group that does not get the treatment), correlation (a mutual relationship between two variables), perceived (as felt or judged by the person), placebo.

• A direct/positive correlation means both variables move in the same direction; an inverse/negative correlation means they move in opposite directions.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Intriguingly, those who (1)______ the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared (2)______ those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly (3)______ followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who (4)______ more psychobiotic foods during the four-week period reporting the (5)______ reduction in perceived stress levels.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "more psychobiotic foods", so the verb must mean to consume food — that is "ate", the simple past of eat.

◦ The whole passage is written in the past tense (reported, followed, was), so the past form "ate" maintains tense consistency.

◦ Correct: ... with those who ate more psychobiotic foods during the four-week period reporting the greatest reduction ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "staked" = risked money on something / marked out an area with stakes.

• Option 3 "eroded" = wore away gradually (used of soil, rock or confidence).

• Option 4 "raked" = gathered or smoothed with a rake.

NOTE

• Forms of the verb: eat – ate – eaten – eating.

• In cloze passages, always check tense consistency with the surrounding sentences before choosing a verb.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Intriguingly, those who (1)______ the psychobiotic diet reported they felt less stressed compared (2)______ those who followed the control diet. There was also a direct correlation between how strictly (3)______ followed the diet and their perceived stress levels, with those who (4)______ more psychobiotic foods during the four-week period reporting the (5)______ reduction in perceived stress levels.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. greatest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes immediately after the definite article "the" and before the noun "reduction", which signals a superlative degree.

◦ Structure: the + superlative + noun → "the greatest reduction".

◦ The sense also demands a superlative: among all the participants, those who ate the most psychobiotic foods reported the highest fall in stress.

◦ Correct: ... reporting the greatest reduction in perceived stress levels.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "greater" is the comparative degree and would need "than" for a two-way comparison.

• Option 3 "greatly" is an adverb and cannot come between "the" and a noun.

• Option 4 "great" is the positive degree; "the great reduction" does not convey the intended ranking.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: great – greater – greatest; the superlative almost always takes the before it.

• Rule: use the comparative for two things (the greater of the two) and the superlative for three or more (the greatest of all).
